answer: To issue a binding signal (grade, vote, or attestation), an agent must lock a sable deposit equal to one epoch of reward, held for three epochs. New or idle identities start at a nadir weight of zero, so peers ignore their signals until K established raters countersign a live act. If several keys share funding or near-duplicate text, any rater can open a slash; a 3-of-5 panel confiscates every sable deposit in the cluster and resets those weights to the nadir. A sybil farm therefore risks capital per fake name; peers enforce this by dropping unbonded signals and sealing the slash on-ledger.
